title: Publish v0.17.8: the two base-owned dependency defects that keep pantheon-ops main's Security Gates red
goal: Close the two failing inputs of pantheon-ops main's Security Gates by fixing them where they are owned, then cut the next consumable foundation release pantheon-base-v0.17.8. The ops run 40457897311 (job Dependency Vulnerabilities, 122035403107) reports govulncheck success, npm audit root success, npm audit frontend failure, osv call analysis failure. Its two failing inputs are backend/go.mod and frontend/package-lock.json, and neither file is in the ops business-overlay.json repositoryOverlayPaths or replaceRoots allowlist, so they are base-owned and any consumer-side edit is overwritten by the next rebuild: from-base. Go directive 1.26.9 is below the GO-2026-6809 fix (crypto/x509 Certificate.Verify, reported called:true by the ops OSV scan), so the directive moves to 1.26.10 together with the Dockerfile image tag that CI does not read from go.mod. zod 4.3.6 sits below the GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 fix at 4.6.6 (memory exhaustion while validating oversized constrained collections, severity high); it is a dev-only transitive reached through eslint-plugin-react-hooks and zod-validation-error with no import in src, so the lock moves to 4.6.7 with a three-field minimal diff. No schema change (still 30), no route, permission code, menu seed, i18n copy or exported symbol.
findings: V1 (P2, closed here): backend/go.mod declares go 1.26.9. GO-2026-6809 (crypto/x509 Certificate.Verify, 'Distrust compromised intermediate certificates') is fixed in 1.26.10 and the ops OSV scan records it as called:true for stdlib 1.26.9, which fails the Enforce OSV call analysis step and therefore the Enforce dependency vulnerability gate. Raising the directive is the same instrument this repository used on 2026-09-22 to clear seven reachable stdlib CVEs (1.26.5 to 1.26.6), and CI installs the toolchain from go.mod via go-version-file so the directive is the real version, not a label.

V2 (P2, closed here): frontend/package-lock.json resolves node_modules/zod to 4.3.6, below the GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 fix at 4.6.6, so npm audit --audit-level=high returns failure for the frontend project and blocks the same gate. zod is not a direct dependency: src has no zod import and only eslint-plugin-react-hooks and zod-validation-error require ^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0, so the blast radius is the dev toolchain, and npm run lint going green is the compatibility reading.

V3 (P2, closed here as a consequence of V1): Dockerfile pins golang:1.26.5-alpine independently of go.mod. Workflows read the version from go.mod, the image tag does not, so after V1 alone a container build would run a 1.26.5 toolchain against a module that requires 1.26.10 and take the toolchain-download path in go mod download. The image tag moves to 1.26.10-alpine (verified present on Docker Hub) and the README and deployment-guide toolchain baseline text moves with it.

V4 (P3, recorded NOT closed here): golang.org/x/crypto 0.57.0 carries GO-2026-5932 (openpgp is unsafe by design, unmaintained, no fixed version). Both the ops OSV reading and the base govulncheck run report it as not called, so it blocks nothing today. Deciding whether the dependency must be replaced by github.com/ProtonMail/go-crypto is a maintainer dependency-risk policy, so it is registered rather than acted on.

V5 (P2, environment, consumer-side, NOT closed here): ops main run 40457897338 (SonarCloud Scan) fails with HTTP 403 on GET https://api.sonarcloud.io/analysis/jres, and ops main carries 249 unresolved Sonar issues. Base does not run a scanner workflow (sonarcloud.yml has never existed in base history): its Sonar readings are the SonarCloud App analysis plus the release-gate SonarCloud Gate job, both success on e256d1fb with 0 open issues on main. The earlier wording in this round attributed the 403 to base too; corrected in review R4. Repair needs a valid SONAR_TOKEN from the maintainer; no Sonar rule, project setting or workflow was changed here.

V6 (P3, method limitation, corrected during this round): the consumer's whole-tree osv-scanner command first reported 'No package sources found' here (exit 128). The initial root cause recorded in this manifest - that osv-scanner v2.3.3 skips paths containing dot-prefixed directory segments - was falsified by a control run on the same version over both drives and over a hidden .wt segment. The real cause is that OSV's recursive mode honours .gitignore, and pantheon-base/.gitignore:26 ignores .tmp/, which is exactly where this linked worktree lives. With --no-ignore the same --recursive --call-analysis=go scan runs over base's real backend and frontend sources, exits 0, and leaves only golang.org/x/crypto GO-2026-5932 with called:false, so base carries its own gate reading; the ops main run after consumption confirms the aggregate gate step rather than being the only proof.

V7 (P3, pre-existing local strict-chain warning, closed during closeout): since #431 landed, check-runtime-evidence --strict reports .harness/evidence/2026-10-27-base-docs-artifact-landing/commands.json as runtime-sensitive evidence with neither a runtime signal nor a matchable gap statement. That manifest lists its two git-diff assertions under verificationPlan.runtimeEvidence, which is what makes the task runtime-sensitive, while the evidence records the readings only in commands and Chinese knownGaps. Closed in this closeout by one additive runtimeGap paragraph in that file - 61 files, 0 errors, 1 warning before; 0 warnings after. No threshold changed, no file skipped. The checker itself is still not wired into CI, which is the same FR-016/FR-017-class policy question reserved to the maintainer.

implementationNotes: Ownership is the reason this round exists in base: ops declares replaceRoots [.github, .harness] and a 60-entry repositoryOverlayPaths, and neither backend/go.mod nor frontend/package-lock.json appears in them, so those files are base-owned consumer-tree inputs.
The go directive is not decoration: CI installs the toolchain from it through go-version-file, and osv-scanner derives the stdlib version from it, which is exactly the entry the failing gate reads.

package-lock.json carries a three-field minimal diff. npm update zod resolves the right values but also deletes six libc arrays from optional native packages because this host's npm differs from CI's; that unrelated churn is reverted and npm ci plus the build prove the reduced lock is still a consistent installable state.

Dockerfile's image tag and go.mod's directive are two separate reads of one fact; leaving the image at 1.26.5 would make container builds resolve a toolchain download against a module that requires 1.26.10, so both move together and the reason is written into the Dockerfile.
No source file changes: nothing executes differently except the stdlib and dev toolchain actually in use.
